interpretation: A complete written independent sentence starts with one of the original 16 resonance markers
A resonance expresses pragmatic stance, not the truth or evidential confidence of its proposition
In nominal morphology, plural `-ri` precedes case `-m`; case slots compete
Verb voice, tense, aspect, modality, and optional manner are ordered slots
Past `-te` and future `-yu` cannot be simultaneously stacked in one tense slot
Progressive `-se`, completive `-mo`, habitual `-në` compete within the aspect slot
Ability `-ki`, permission `-ho`, and obligation `-du` are *different meanings* and occupy one slot
A negator `nu` immediately preceding a predicate negates that predicate's proposition
A polar question ends in `he`; a request/command uses `ya`, never both in one independent finite clause
contrastive_example: `hë ti haro he?` vs `hë ti haro ya?`
status: Preserved written rule; context may distinguish requests

interpretation: Direct observation `si`, reported `hu`, inferred `ye` indicate **information source**, not truth
An evidential is placed after the finite predicate, before a final question/request particle in a simple clause
status: Editorial syntax specification; needs full quote-scope testing

interpretation: Direct objects use `-m`, recipients `-tu`, companions `-wa`; one suffix cannot represent all these roles
status: Preserved semantic roles; some ditransitive structures remain unreviewed

interpretation: English *you* and *them* are not interchangeable when source explicitly marks `ti-wa`
status: Strong editorial correction candidate; review in discourse

interpretation: A single sentence can be literally accurate but omit evidence, aspect, or interpersonal tone in a natural contextual translation
contrastive_example: `sen mi goro-ki.` → “I can fly.” / “I can.” with prior context

interpretation: If an engine cannot parse a sentence, that does **not** establish the sentence is ungrammatical
contrastive_example: `zher mi nu këmiro.` is a simple negative even when its English gloss is elliptical

interpretation: Contextually supplied quantifiers, extra motives, and added agents should be annotated separately from literal translation
contrastive_example: “I will buy the book” vs “Possibly, but I want to ask something first”
status: Review rule, not automatic source rewriting

interpretation: Quoted independent sentences may have their own resonance; a random mid-clause marker does not start a new argument
Conditionals `wë`, purpose `ko`, reasons `ro` and reports `do` delimit propositions whose scope can change truth conditions
contrastive_example: “If X, Y” does not assert X
status: Preserved semantics; full formal parser pending

interpretation: A negative followed by a positive claim in the same conversation might be a correction or update, not automatically a contradiction
contrastive_example: “I didn't see it.” / “I did see it after looking again.”

interpretation: Contextual paraphrases, and unapproved candidate idioms/sense notes, never silently overwrite canonical entries
